- To understand what the wrapped model actually computes per replica, start with [Architecture Overview](5-architecture-overview) and the fusion mechanics in [Residual Fusion Design](6-residual-fusion-design).
- For the loss terms summed in `loss_fct` under parallelism, see [Prediction Decoder and Loss](11-prediction-decoder-and-loss).
- To interpret the MoE balance-loss statistics logged during parallel training, see [Soft Router and Balance Loss](8-soft-router-and-balance-loss).
- For the full flag inventory including `--multi-gpu` and `--device-ids`, see [Training and Prediction Commands](4-training-and-prediction-commands) and [Configuration Reference](19-configuration-reference).

# Unseen Perturbation Inference



This page explains how DyMoE-Pert produces transcriptomic response predictions for perturbations that were **never observed during training** — a novel single gene, or a gene combination whose joint effect the model has no direct supervision for. The central design insight is that perturbation identity is carried by *gene names resolved against precomputed, name-keyed embedding tables*, not by learned row indices bound to the training perturbation set. This is what makes zero-shot generalization structurally possible. We cover the CLI entry point, the `predict()` pipeline, the embedding composition mechanism, checkpoint loading, interaction analysis, and batch evaluation on unseen splits.

Sources: [scripts/infer.py](scripts/infer.py#L1-L4), [models/model.py](models/model.py#L379-L386)

## What "Unseen" Means at Inference Time

An unseen perturbation is any condition string such as `CEBPA+ctrl` (a single perturbation) or `CEBPA+JUN` (a combination) that does not appear in the training split. The parsing utility `parse_any_pert` accepts *arbitrary* gene-name strings: single perturbations of the form `GENE+ctrl` reduce to `[GENE]`, while combinations reduce to `[GENE1, GENE2]`. Nothing in this path is restricted to genes or combinations seen during training — the condition is treated purely as data, not as a lookup into a fixed vocabulary. Similarly, when a prediction cell graph is constructed, the `pert_idx` field is explicitly set to `None` and the perturbation is attached as a name string (`pert=pert_gene`), meaning prediction inputs carry no dependency on the training-time perturbation index space.

Sources: [models/utils.py](models/utils.py#L34-L39), [models/utils.py](models/utils.py#L462-L472)

## Entry Point: `scripts/infer.py`

The dedicated inference script predicts one single-gene or double-gene perturbation from a trained checkpoint produced by `train.py`. After resolving the device and validating that the embedding file, `config.pkl`, and `model.pt` all exist, it loads the dataset with `data.prepare_split(split="no_test", seed=77)` — notably *without* a test split, since prediction here is user-directed rather than benchmark-driven. It then instantiates the `scPert` wrapper, restores the checkpoint via `load_pretrained`, and calls `model.predict([args.perturbation], num_samples=args.num_cells, batch_size=args.batch_size)`. The result is persisted as `pred_dymoe_{pert_key}.npz`, where `+` characters in the condition name are replaced with underscores.

| CLI Parameter | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--data-name` | `norman` | Dataset key; selects the matching scGPT embedding file |
| `--data-path` | `./data` | Location of GEARS-format data |
| `--embedding-dir` | `./embeddings` | Directory holding gene embedding `.npy` files |
| `--checkpoint` | *(required)* | Directory containing `config.pkl` and `model.pt` |
| `--perturbation` | *(required)* | Condition string, e.g. `CEBPA+ctrl` or `CEBPA+JUN` |
| `--device` | `auto` | `auto`, `cpu`, or `cuda:N` |
| `--num-cells` | `32` | Control cells sampled per perturbation |
| `--batch-size` | `8` | Cells per inference forward pass |

The `EMBEDDING_FILES` mapping hard-couples each dataset name to its 512-dimensional scGPT embedding file, guaranteeing the model is constructed with the same embedding table it was trained with.

Sources: [scripts/infer.py](scripts/infer.py#L16-L22), [scripts/infer.py](scripts/infer.py#L25-L37), [scripts/infer.py](scripts/infer.py#L47-L54), [scripts/infer.py](scripts/infer.py#L56-L72), [scripts/infer.py](scripts/infer.py#L73-L76)

## The `predict()` Pipeline

`scPert.predict(pert_list, num_samples, batch_size)` operates in five stages. First, the control population is isolated (`self.adata.obs['condition'] == 'ctrl'`) and the best model is moved to device and set to `eval()` mode. Second, each requested condition is normalized to a key (`+` → `_`) and checked against the in-memory `saved_pred` cache, so repeated queries for the same perturbation are free. Third, `create_cell_graph_dataset_for_prediction` samples `num_samples` random control cells and wraps each one in its own graph tagged with the target perturbation name. Fourth, graphs are streamed through a PyG `DataLoader` under `torch.no_grad()`, and the model output is split via `_split_model_output` — discarding the MoE auxiliary statistics (`router weights`, `balance loss`) that are only meaningful during training. Fifth, per-cell predictions are averaged into a single mean transcriptome, and both the mean and the full per-cell array (under an `all_{pert}` key) are cached and written to disk.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[CLI: --perturbation CEBPA+JUN] --> B[parse_any_pert\ncondition string to gene list]
    B --> C{saved_pred cache\nhit?}
    C -- hit --> D[return cached result]
    C -- miss --> E[Sample num_cells ctrl cells\nfrom ctrl_adata]
    E --> F[Build one PyG graph per cell\nx = expression, pert = name,\npert_idx = None]
    F --> G[DataLoader batches\nmodel.eval + no_grad]
    G --> H[scPert_Model forward\nname-keyed embedding lookup]
    H --> I[_split_model_output\nkeep pred, drop MoE aux]
    I --> J[Mean over per-cell predictions]
    J --> K[Cache in saved_pred\n+ save pred_dymoe_key.npz]
```

This per-cell sampling design matters: because control cells vary, the mean prediction is a Monte Carlo estimate over the control population rather than a single deterministic forward pass. A larger `--num-cells` therefore reduces sampling variance at linear cost.

Sources: [models/scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L424-L447), [models/scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L449-L452), [models/scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L456-L470), [models/scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L472-L485), [models/scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L487-L491), [models/inference.py](models/inference.py#L37-L40)

## Zero-Shot Embedding Composition

The mechanism that makes unseen perturbations addressable lives in `scPert_Model.__init__`. Instead of relying solely on `nn.Embedding` rows indexed by training-time perturbation IDs, the model registers two **precomputed, name-keyed lookup buffers**: KG gene embeddings from `gene_2_kge_comgcn_final_common.npz` (128-dimensional knowledge-graph embeddings) and perturbation embeddings from `gene_embeddingss_full_common.npz`, each accompanied by a `gene`-name → index dictionary built at load time. Because the dictionaries cover the perturbation gene space by name, a novel combination like `CEBPA+JUN` resolves through the same lookup path as a training perturbation — the model never needs to have "seen" the pair. The 512-dimensional scGPT gene embeddings (`gene_emb`) are loaded from the dataset-specific file supplied via `embedding_path`.

These two branches feed the fusion layer: with MoE fusion enabled, `ResidualMoEFusion` receives the KG and scGPT branches and blends a shared base MLP with three experts (KG, scGPT, interaction) through softmax router weights, producing `output_norm(h_base + expert_output)`; without MoE, the 128-dim KG and 512-dim scGPT vectors are simply concatenated into the 640-dimensional input expected by `pert_dense`. In both cases the fusion is *compositional over genes*, which is the property that transfers to unseen combinations.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NameKeyed["Name-keyed precomputed tables"]
        KGE[KG embeddings\n128-d\ncomgcn KGE npz]
        SCE[scGPT embeddings\n512-d\ndataset npy]
        PE[Perturbation embeddings\nfull_common npz]
    end
    subgraph Fusion
        BASE[Base MLP on concat] --> ADD((+))
        E1[KG expert] --> W
        E2[scGPT expert] --> W[Router softmax\nweighted sum]
        E3[Interaction expert] --> W
        W --> ADD
        ADD --> NORM[LayerNorm]
    end
    KGE --> BASE
    SCE --> BASE
    KGE --> E1
    SCE --> E2
    KGE --> E3
    SCE --> E3
    NORM --> P[Perturbation representation\nfor unseen combo]
```

> [!TIP]
> The critical enabler is the pair of facts verified in code: prediction graphs set `pert_idx=None` and carry only the perturbation *name* (models/utils.py#L462-L472), while the embedding tables are indexed by gene *name* dictionaries (models/model.py#L377-L386). Identity flows through strings end-to-end, so the index space learned during training never becomes a hard constraint at inference.

Sources: [models/model.py](models/model.py#L370-L390), [models/model.py](models/model.py#L408-L414), [models/model.py](models/model.py#L478-L490), [models/model.py](models/model.py#L285-L311)

## Loading Checkpoints Safely

`load_pretrained` reconstructs the exact training configuration before restoring weights. It reads `config.pkl`, strips keys that `model_initialize` does not accept or that must be re-derived from the freshly loaded data (`device`, `num_genes`, `num_perts`, `embedding_size`, `pert_names`, `pert_node_map`), and drops legacy uncertainty fields if present. The `model.pt` state dict is always loaded onto CPU first; if the checkpoint was saved from a DataParallel run, the `module.` prefix is removed from every key before `load_state_dict`. Finally the model is moved to the target device and aliased as `best_model`, which is the object `predict()` uses — meaning inference always runs against the best-validation checkpoint semantics, never the last-step weights.

Sources: [models/scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L357-L397), [models/scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L399-L422)

## From Prediction to Interaction Analysis: `GI_predict`

For combinatorial perturbations, `GI_predict(combo)` turns raw predictions into quantitative genetic-interaction parameters. It requests three conditions through the same unseen-perturbation pipeline: `G1+ctrl`, `G2+ctrl`, and `G1+G2` (reusing the `saved_pred` cache when available). Each predicted mean expression is control-centered by subtracting `get_mean_control`, optionally restricted to a curated set of high-expression GI genes, and then passed to `get_GI_params`, which fits a Theil–Sen regression of the double-perturbation response on the two single responses. The fitted coefficients yield epistasis-relevant quantities: interaction magnitudes (`mag`), dominance (`dominance`), equality of contribution (`eq_contr`), and distance correlations. In other words, the same zero-shot predictor that emits a transcriptome also composes into an interaction-score calculator for pairs the model never jointly observed.

Sources: [models/scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L494-L530), [models/utils.py](models/utils.py#L493-L526), [models/utils.py](models/utils.py#L528-L542), [models/utils.py](models/utils.py#L560-L565)

## Batch Evaluation on Unseen Splits

Where `predict()` serves targeted queries, `evaluate()` in `models/inference.py` scores the *test loader* — which, under the simulation split, contains held-out unseen combinations. It mirrors the prediction path's discipline: `model.eval()`, per-batch device transfer via `_prepare_batch` (which reassembles PyG batches from per-cell lists under parallel wrappers), and a `torch.no_grad()` forward. Alongside predictions and ground truth it captures `de_idx` per cell so differential-expression genes can be sliced out for focused metrics. `compute_metrics` then aggregates per-perturbation MSE and Pearson correlation — including the `_de` variants computed only on DE genes and only for non-control perturbations — over the mean of per-cell predictions, matching the aggregation used by `predict()`.

| Aspect | `predict()` | `evaluate()` |
|---|---|---|
| Input | Arbitrary condition strings | Pre-built test loader |
| Control cells | Randomly sampled at call time | Fixed test-set cells |
| Ground truth | Not required | Required for metrics |
| Output | Mean + per-cell predictions, npz artifact | `pert_cat` / `pred` / `truth` / DE slices |
| Typical split | Any (`no_test` in the CLI) | `simulation` with unseen-combination subgroups |

Subgroup analysis over unseen-combination categories is triggered automatically after training when `split == 'simulation'`, reporting per-subgroup test metrics — the split mechanics themselves are covered in [Perturbation Splits and Simulation Split](14-perturbation-splits-and-simulation-split), and the downstream DE-gene analysis in [Metrics and DE Gene Analysis](18-metrics-and-de-gene-analysis).

Sources: [models/inference.py](models/inference.py#L42-L87), [models/inference.py](models/inference.py#L89-L145), [models/inference.py](models/inference.py#L22-L34), [models/scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L697-L717)

## Practical Checklist

- **Always pass the same `--embedding-dir`** used at training time; `model.pt` assumes the scGPT table matches, and the KG/perturbation tables are loaded from fixed paths under `./embeddings` inside the model constructor.
- **Raise `--num-cells` for stable point estimates**; the mean prediction is a sample average over control cells, and `GI_predict` interactions inherit that variance.
- **Reuse `saved_pred` deliberately** — the cache keyed by condition string makes repeated singles/combo queries cheap, and `GI_predict` depends on it for its three-condition fetch.
- **Check the MoE stats before trusting a prediction** — `predict()` discards router auxiliaries, but the ablation mode and expert configuration embedded in `config.pkl` determine which branches contributed; see [Ablation Modes Framework](9-ablation-modes-framework) and [Configuration Reference](19-configuration-reference).

Sources: [scripts/infer.py](scripts/infer.py#L47-L54), [models/model.py](models/model.py#L371-L390), [models/scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L466-L470), [models/scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L511-L518)

## Where to Go Next

To understand how the test set is constructed so that specific combinations are guaranteed unseen, read [Perturbation Splits and Simulation Split](14-perturbation-splits-and-simulation-split). For the router and expert machinery referenced throughout this page, see [Residual Fusion Design](6-residual-fusion-design) and [Soft Router and Balance Loss](8-soft-router-and-balance-loss). To interpret evaluation numbers on unseen splits, continue to [Metrics and DE Gene Analysis](18-metrics-and-de-gene-analysis), and for runnable end-to-end commands, see [Training and Prediction Commands](4-training-and-prediction-commands).

# Metrics and DE Gene Analysis



This page documents the evaluation system of DyMoE-Pert: how differentially expressed (DE) genes are computed and stored, how predictions are collected into comparable result structures, and how the layered metric suites — standard per-perturbation scores, deeper DE analyses, non-dropout / non-zero analyses, and simulation-split subgroup breakdowns — are orchestrated inside `scPert.train()`. If [Training Loop Orchestration](15-training-loop-orchestration) covers how the model learns, this page covers how the repository decides whether the learning was *biologically meaningful*: performance is measured primarily on the top-ranked DE genes for each perturbation, not on all genes uniformly.

## The Evaluation Architecture at a Glance

The metrics system follows a three-stage design that cleanly separates *data provenance*, *result collection*, and *metric computation*. DE gene identities are computed once during dataset processing and persisted inside the AnnData object; the evaluator harvests prediction slices per cell at batch time; and metric functions operate purely on those cached arrays. Understanding this flow first makes every subsequent function self-explanatory:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["scanpy<br/>rank_genes_groups"] --> B["adata.uns<br/>rank_genes_groups_cov_all<br/>(full gene ranking)"]
    B --> C["get_dropout_non_zero_genes<br/>top 20 non-zero /<br/>non-dropout DE sets"]
    C --> D["PyG Data objects<br/>each cell carries de_idx"]
    D --> E["evaluate()<br/>pred / truth / pred_de / truth_de"]
    E --> F["compute_metrics<br/>MSE + Pearson,<br/>all genes & DE genes"]
    E --> G["deeper_analysis<br/>direction, delta, fold-change,<br/>top 20/50/100/200"]
    E --> H["non_dropout_analysis<br/>dropout-aware direction<br/>& sigma metrics"]
    F --> I["Checkpoint selection<br/>min val mse_de"]
    G --> J["Simulation-split<br/>subgroup aggregation"]
    H --> J
```

**Prerequisite note**: the diagram introduces one vocabulary item you will see everywhere — `adata.uns` is scanpy's "unstructured annotations" slot, and DyMoE-Pert uses it as the canonical registry for DE gene sets keyed by full condition names like `cell_type_pert_1+1`. Every metric function in `models/inference.py` re-derives gene indices by looking conditions up in this registry, so the registry must exist before evaluation runs.

The pipeline begins in the data layer, where `new_data_process` invokes `get_DE_genes` and then `get_dropout_non_zero_genes` before persisting `perturb_processed.h5ad`. This means the DE gene sets used at evaluation time are frozen into the dataset artifact itself, guaranteeing that train/val/test evaluation uses identical gene definitions.

Sources: [data_utils.py](models/data_utils.py#L15-L70), [ProcePertdata.py](models/ProcePertdata.py#L217-L266), [inference.py](models/inference.py#L42-L87)

## Stage 1: Computing and Registering DE Genes

DE gene identification lives in `models/data_utils.py` and is a two-pass process. The first pass, `rank_genes_groups_by_cov`, wraps scanpy's `sc.tl.rank_genes_groups` and runs it **per cell-type covariate**: for each `cell_type` category it subsets the AnnData, compares each perturbed condition against its matched control (`_'.join([cov_cat, 'ctrl'])`), and ranks genes by *absolute* score (`rankby_abs=True`) so that both up- and down-regulated genes compete on equal footing. The full ranking — not just the top slice — is written back into `adata.uns[key_added]` with `n_genes=len(adata.var)`, which later allows any cutoff depth (20/50/100/200) to be derived from the same registry.

The public entry point `get_DE_genes` prepares the grouping columns (`dose_val`, `control`, `condition_name`) and then calls this ranking with `key_added='rank_genes_groups_cov_all'`. The `skip_calc_de` flag bypasses recomputation when the h5ad already carries the annotation — a meaningful saving since ranking all genes for every condition is the most expensive step of preprocessing.

| Function | Role | Output location |
|---|---|---|
| `rank_genes_groups_by_cov` | Per-cell-type DE ranking vs matched control | `adata.uns['rank_genes_groups_cov_all']` |
| `get_DE_genes` | Column prep + full-gene ranking entry point | same, via `key_added` |
| `get_dropout_non_zero_genes` | Filters DE ranking through expression masks | `adata.uns['top_non_zero_de_20']`, `top_non_dropout_de_20`, `non_zeros_gene_idx`, `non_dropout_gene_idx` |

Sources: [data_utils.py](models/data_utils.py#L15-L70)

The second pass, `get_dropout_non_zero_genes`, addresses a scRNA-seq-specific pitfall: **dropout**. A gene observed as zero under perturbation may be a biological zero or a sequencing dropout, and evaluating on a dropout-contaminated DE set corrupts metrics. The function partitions genes per perturbation into `non_zero` (nonzero mean expression under the perturbation), `true_zeros` (zero in *both* perturbed and control means), and their union `non_dropouts`. It then intersects the top-ranked DE list with these masks to emit two 20-gene subsets — `top_non_zero_de_20` and `top_non_dropout_de_20` — plus the full index sets, all stored in `adata.uns`.

> [!TIP]
> The distinction between "observed zero" and "true zero" (zero in both perturbed *and* control means) is what makes `non_dropout_analysis` trustworthy: genes that are zero in the control cannot show a spurious direction change, so direction-accuracy metrics on the non-dropout set measure biology rather than measurement noise. When interpreting `frac_correct_direction_non_dropout`, remember its denominator is the union set, not the top-20 slice.

Sources: [data_utils.py](models/data_utils.py#L72-L132)

Finally, these annotations travel with the training data. Each PyG `Data` object exposes `pert`, `y`, and `de_idx` — the per-cell DE gene index slice — which is how the evaluator knows which genes matter for a given cell without re-querying the AnnData at batch time.

Sources: [ProcePertdata.py](models/ProcePertdata.py#L198-L215), [inference.py](models/inference.py#L22-L34)

## Stage 2: Collecting Predictions with `evaluate`

`evaluate(loader, model, device)` is the single ingestion point for all downstream metrics. It runs the model in `torch.no_grad()` mode over a loader and accumulates four aligned arrays: `pred` and `truth` over all genes, and `pred_de` / `truth_de` containing only the DE slice for each cell — extracted at line 72–74 as `p[idx, de_genes]` using the per-item `de_idx`. The returned dictionary is the contract every metric function depends on:

| Key | Shape | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `pert_cat` | `(N,)` | Perturbation label per cell |
| `pred` / `truth` | `(N, G)` | Predicted / true expression, all genes |
| `pred_de` / `truth_de` | `(N, 20)` | Predicted / true expression, top-20 DE genes only |

Two implementation details matter for developers extending this path. First, `_prepare_batch` normalizes both single-GPU batches and `DataListLoader` lists (PyG `DataParallel` setups), so `evaluate` is multi-GPU-transparent; second, `_split_model_output` strips the MoE auxiliary dictionary from the model's tuple output so the evaluator always sees the pure prediction tensor regardless of ablation mode.

Sources: [inference.py](models/inference.py#L42-L87)

## Stage 3: The Metric Suites

### Standard metrics: `compute_metrics`

`compute_metrics(results)` produces the headline numbers. For each unique perturbation it computes the **mean prediction vs. mean truth** across that perturbation's cells — evaluating on population-level profiles, which is the convention inherited from GEARS-style evaluation — and calculates MSE and Pearson correlation twice: once on all genes, once on the top-20 DE slice. Pearson failures from constant vectors are coerced to `0` to keep aggregation robust. The `ctrl` perturbation is excluded from DE-metric aggregation (a control has no meaningful DE set) but still receives all-gene scores.

| Metric key | Scope | Aggregation |
|---|---|---|
| `mse`, `pearson` | All genes | Mean over perturbations |
| `mse_de`, `pearson_de` | Top-20 DE genes | Mean over non-control perturbations |
| `metrics_pert[pert][...]` | Per-perturbation | Returned separately for subgroup analysis |

Sources: [inference.py](models/inference.py#L89-L145)

### The comprehensive suite: `deeper_analysis`

`deeper_analysis(adata, test_res)` is the workhorse for paper-grade reporting, computing roughly forty per-perturbation statistics. Its gene-set resolution strategy is the defining feature: instead of a single DE slice, it materializes the top **20, 50, 100, and 200** genes from `rank_genes_groups_cov_all` simultaneously, then reports metrics at every depth. This exposes the *scaling behavior* of model quality — a model can look strong at 20 genes while degrading rapidly at 200, or vice versa.

Its metric families are:

| Family | Example keys | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Direction accuracy | `frac_correct_direction_20/50/100/200`, `frac_correct_direction_all` | Fraction of genes where `sign(pred − ctrl) == sign(truth − ctrl)` |
| Coverage intervals | `frac_in_range`, `frac_in_range_45_55`, `frac_in_range_40_60`, `frac_in_range_25_75` | Fraction of predicted DE means falling inside truth quantile bands (calibrated uncertainty) |
| Sigma statistics | `mean_sigma`, `std_sigma`, `frac_sigma_below_1/2` | Distance of prediction from truth mean in units of truth std |
| Delta correlation | `pearson_delta`, `pearson_delta_de`, `pearson_delta_top20/50/100/200_de` | Correlation on *change from control*, isolating perturbation response from baseline |
| Fold-change gaps | `fold_change_gap_upreg_3`, `_upreg_10`, `_downreg_0.33`, `_downreg_0.1` | Mean absolute gap between predicted and true fold-change ratios in strong-FC regimes |
| HVG metrics | `pearson_top200_hvg`, `pearson_delta_top200_hvg` | Same scores on the 200 most-variable genes (dataset-wide, perturbation-agnostic) |

The delta variants deserve emphasis: by subtracting `ctrl` from both prediction and truth before correlating, they remove the dominant shared baseline and reward the model specifically for capturing the perturbation-induced shift — the quantity that actually matters for `sensitivity` claims. Fold-change gaps are guarded by expression floors (`pert_mean < 0.5` entries are zeroed out of the ratio) to avoid meaningless divisions near zero.

Sources: [inference.py](models/inference.py#L384-L649)

### Dropout-aware suites: `non_dropout_analysis` and `non_zero_analysis`

These two functions apply the same metric machinery but over the dropout-filtered gene sets registered earlier. `non_dropout_analysis` computes direction accuracy at **three scopes** per perturbation — top-20 non-dropout DE genes, all non-zero genes, and all non-dropout genes — giving a coarse-to-fine view of directional fidelity, then adds the familiar in-range/sigma/delta families on the 20-gene slice. `non_zero_analysis` is its non-zero-only counterpart using `top_non_zero_de_20`.

| Function | Gene registry used | Distinct value |
|---|---|---|
| `non_dropout_analysis` | `top_non_dropout_de_20`, `non_zeros_gene_idx`, `non_dropout_gene_idx` | Direction accuracy over *all* non-dropout genes, not just top-20 |
| `non_zero_analysis` | `top_non_zero_de_20` | Direction and delta metrics on expression-confirmed genes only |

Both functions reconstruct the per-condition control mean directly from `adata.X` rather than from the results dictionary, so they require the full AnnData to be in scope — a deliberate coupling that keeps the control reference consistent with training-time `ctrl_expression`.

Sources: [inference.py](models/inference.py#L148-L382)

## Stage 4: Orchestration in `scPert.train()`

The evaluation stack is wired into the training loop, not bolted on afterwards. At the end of **every epoch**, `train()` runs `evaluate` over both train and val loaders and reduces them via `compute_metrics`, logging Overall MSE and Top-20 DE MSE for both splits (and the full metric set to W&B when enabled). Then comes the decision that shapes the whole experiment:

```python
if val_metrics['mse_de'] < min_val:
    min_val = val_metrics['mse_de']
    best_model = deepcopy(_unwrap_parallel_model(self.model)).cpu()
```

**Model selection is driven by validation top-20 DE MSE — not overall MSE.** This is a deliberate design stance: a model can minimize genome-wide reconstruction error by reproducing the control baseline while missing the actual perturbation response on the genes that respond. Selecting on `mse_de` optimizes exactly the axis the DE registry defines as biologically important.

> [!TIP]
> When reproducing ablation results, be aware that early-stopping behavior differs between metrics: two models with near-identical overall MSE can have materially different `mse_de` trajectories, especially in the first few epochs as the MoE router converges. Comparing runs requires holding the selection metric (`mse_de`) fixed, not the overall MSE.

After training, if a `test_loader` exists, the best model is re-wrapped for parallel inference, evaluated once, and the terminal metrics are printed. The post-hoc layer then runs `deeper_analysis` and `non_dropout_analysis` on the test results, and the code highlights a compact reporting set — `pearson_delta` plus three non-dropout statistics (`frac_opposite_direction_top20_non_dropout`, `frac_sigma_below_1_non_dropout`, `mse_top20_de_non_dropout`) — which mirrors the standard reporting table used to compare against GEARS and scPert baselines.

Sources: [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L620-L695)

### Subgroup breakdown for simulation splits

When the split is `simulation` (see [Perturbation Splits and Simulation Split](14-perturbation-splits-and-simulation-split)), the test perturbations belong to named subgroups (e.g., unseen-single, unseen-combo). The training loop aggregates both `test_pert_res` (from `compute_metrics`) and the deeper/non-dropout outputs **per subgroup**, averaging each metric across its member perturbations and printing/logging results as `test_{subgroup}_{metric}`. This is the mechanism behind the headline generalization claims of the model: it separates performance on truly unseen genetic interactions from performance on combinations merely unseen as pairs.

Sources: [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L697-L744)

## Producing Artifacts for Custom Analysis

The prediction path complements the metric path. `scripts/infer.py` loads a checkpoint via `model.load_pretrained`, runs `model.predict([perturbation])` over replicated control cells, and saves the output as `pred_dymoe_{pert}.npz` containing both the per-cell predictions (`all_*` key) and the cell-mean prediction. These artifacts are designed for downstream users who want to apply the same `deeper_analysis` machinery to their own perturbation lists without rerunning training — pair the saved arrays with an AnnData carrying the DE registry and the full metric suite is available offline.

Sources: [infer.py](scripts/infer.py#L56-L76)

## Practical Recipe: Running the Full Evaluation Stack

The minimal end-to-end sequence, mirroring what `scPert.train()` performs internally:

```python
from models.inference import evaluate, compute_metrics, deeper_analysis, non_dropout_analysis

test_res = evaluate(test_loader, best_model, device)       # collect pred/truth/pred_de/truth_de
metrics, per_pert = compute_metrics(test_res)              # headline MSE/Pearson, all + DE
out_deep = deeper_analysis(data.adata, test_res)           # direction/delta/fold-change at 20–200
out_ndrop = non_dropout_analysis(data.adata, test_res)     # dropout-robust direction + sigma
```

Requirements for this to work unchanged: the AnnData must have been processed through `new_data_process` (so `rank_genes_groups_cov_all` and the non-dropout keys exist in `adata.uns`), and the loader must yield items exposing `de_idx`. If you bring a custom dataset, the DE registry is built automatically — see [GEARS-Format Data Pipeline](12-gears-format-data-pipeline) for the ingestion contract.

| Step | Function | Mandatory input |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `evaluate` | loader, model, device; items carry `de_idx` |
| 2 | `compute_metrics` | results dict from step 1 |
| 3 | `deeper_analysis` | results dict + AnnData with `rank_genes_groups_cov_all` |
| 4 | `non_dropout_analysis` | results dict + AnnData with non-dropout `uns` keys |

Sources: [inference.py](models/inference.py#L42-L87), [ProcePertdata.py](models/ProcePertdata.py#L250-L252)

## Where to Go Next

For the inference-side counterpart of this machinery — how `predict` replicates control cells and how unseen perturbations are scored outside the training loop — continue to [Unseen Perturbation Inference](17-unseen-perturbation-inference). To understand how the loss function mirrors this evaluation philosophy (focal reweighting of DE genes during training), see [Prediction Decoder and Loss](11-prediction-decoder-and-loss). For every hyperparameter referenced by the subgroup analysis and wandb logging, consult [Configuration Reference](19-configuration-reference).

# Configuration Reference



This page is the complete operational reference for every configurable knob in DyMoE-Pert: the command-line arguments of the two entry scripts, the `model_initialize` configuration dictionary that is persisted to checkpoints, the data-pipeline parameters that control dataset loading and splitting, and the set of deliberately hardcoded constants that shape the architecture. Configuration here is not a config file or YAML system — it is a layered chain of Python defaults, where CLI arguments override API defaults, and cross-layer validation rules silently coerce certain values before they ever reach the model. Understanding this precedence chain is the prerequisite for reproducing training runs and correctly restoring checkpoints.

Sources: [train.py](scripts/train.py#L21-L54), [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L271-L354), [model.py](models/model.py#L349-L476)

## Configuration Architecture at a Glance

Configuration flows through four layers, each adding defaults, validation, or coercion. The CLI layer is the outermost; the `scPert_Model` constructor is the innermost consumer. Two properties of this chain matter in practice: first, the model configuration dictionary (`self.config`) is fully serialized with `pickle` into `config.pkl`, so inference never re-specifies model hyperparameters; second, several MoE-related values are coerced at multiple layers simultaneously, which means the *same* constraint appears in `scripts/train.py`, `models/scpert.py`, and `models/model.py` — defense in depth that guarantees an invalid combination cannot be constructed.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["CLI Layer<br/>scripts/train.py<br/>parse_args()"] -->|"attribute per arg"| B["main() coercion<br/>use_moe_fusion=True<br/>balance-weight → 0.0 for controls"]
    B -->|"data args"| C["PertData<br/>load / prepare_split /<br/>get_dataloader"]
    B -->|"hyperparameters"| D["scPert.model_initialize()<br/>config dict built"]
    C -->|"num_genes, num_perts,<br/>node maps"| D
    D -->|"self.config"| E["scPert_Model(args)<br/>config consumed,<br/>moe_hidden_dim resolved"]
    E -->|"save_model()"| F[("checkpoint/<br/>config.pkl + model.pt")]
    F -->|"load_pretrained()<br/>strip runtime keys"| E
```

Sources: [train.py](scripts/train.py#L71-L76), [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L327-L354), [model.py](models/model.py#L357-L368), [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L399-L422)

## Training Script CLI Reference

`scripts/train.py` exposes the complete training configuration surface through `argparse`. The table below lists every argument, its default, and its downstream destination. Note the asymmetry between CLI defaults and API defaults documented later: the CLI tunes `--moe-balance-weight` to `0.0` while the API-level `model_initialize` defaults to `0.01`, and the CLI's `use_moe_fusion` is hardcoded to `True` at `main()` line 73 — there is no flag to disable MoE fusion through the script.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description / Destination |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--data-name` | choice | `norman` | One of the five `EMBEDDING_FILES` keys; selects dataset and default embedding file |
| `--data-path` | str | `./data` | Root directory for downloaded/processed datasets → `PertData` |
| `--embedding-dir` | str | `./embeddings` | Directory joined with the embedding filename |
| `--embedding-file` | str | `None` | Overrides the dataset-aligned embedding file from `EMBEDDING_FILES` |
| `--device` | str | `auto` | `auto`/`cpu`/`cuda`/`cuda:N`; resolved by `resolve_device()` |
| `--batch-size` | int | `64` | Train loader batch size |
| `--test-batch-size` | int | `None` | Falls back to `--batch-size` when unset |
| `--hidden-size` | int | `64` | Backbone hidden dimension; also MoE default when `--moe-hidden-dim` unset |
| `--epochs` | int | `25` | Passed to `scPert.train()` |
| `--lr` | float | `0.001` | Learning rate passed to `scPert.train()` |
| `--seed` | int | `77` | Passed to `prepare_split` |
| `--split` | str | `simulation` | Split strategy name → `prepare_split` |
| `--model-save-name` | str | `None` | Checkpoint directory; defaults to `{data_name}_model_FINAL` |
| `--multi-gpu` | flag | off | Enables PyG `DataParallel` with `DataListLoader` |
| `--device-ids` | str | `0,1,2,3` | Comma-separated GPU ids; `auto`/`all` selects all visible GPUs |
| `--moe-hidden-dim` | int | `None` | MoE fusion hidden dim; `None` resolves to `hidden_size` inside the model |
| `--moe-dropout` | float | `0.1` | Dropout inside MoE projectors, experts, router |
| `--moe-balance-weight` | float | `0.0` | Weight of router balance loss in total loss |
| `--moe-ablation-mode` | choice | `full` | `full`, `base_only`, `no_interaction`, `experts_only` |
| `--moe-router-mode` | choice | `dynamic` | `dynamic` or `fixed_uniform` (strict E3 control) |
| `--no-moe-router-stats` | flag | off | Disables returning/logging MoE router statistics |

Sources: [train.py](scripts/train.py#L21-L54), [train.py](scripts/train.py#L100-L105)

### Dataset–Embedding Binding

The `EMBEDDING_FILES` dictionary enforces a one-to-one pairing between dataset names and pre-computed scGPT embedding files. If `--embedding-file` is provided it overrides the pairing, which is the supported path for experimenting with alternative embeddings. Missing files raise `FileNotFoundError` before any training begins:

| `--data-name` | Bound embedding file |
|---|---|
| `norman` | `gene_embeddings_norman_512.npy` |
| `dixit` | `gene_embeddings_dixit_512.npy` |
| `adamson` | `gene_embeddings_adamson_512.npy` |
| `replogle_k562_essential` | `gene_embeddings_replogle_k562_essential_512.npy` |
| `replogle_rpe1_essential` | `gene_embeddings_replogle_rpe1_essential_512.npy` |

Sources: [train.py](scripts/train.py#L12-L18), [train.py](scripts/train.py#L102-L105), [infer.py](scripts/infer.py#L16-L22)

## Cross-Layer Constraint and Precedence Rules

This is the most consequential section of the reference. Three rules are enforced at multiple layers, and knowing them prevents silent behavioral surprises:

1. **MoE fusion is always on via CLI.** `main()` sets `args.use_moe_fusion = True` unconditionally; the API-level default in `model_initialize` is `False`, so only direct API users can train without the fusion module.
2. **Balance loss is forced to zero for control modes.** When `--moe-router-mode fixed_uniform` or `--moe-ablation-mode base_only` is active, the balance loss is meaningless (no routing entropy to regularize), so `moe_balance_weight` is coerced to `0.0` — first in `train.py main()`, again in `model_initialize`, and a third time in `scPert_Model.__init__`.
3. **Router/ablation mode whitelisting.** Both `model_initialize` and `ResidualMoEFusion` raise `ValueError` for modes outside the accepted sets, so invalid values fail fast at construction.

A precedence table summarizes who wins when values conflict across layers:

| Configuration aspect | Precedence order (highest first) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| MoE hidden dim | CLI `--moe-hidden-dim` → `hidden_size` (resolved in model) | [model.py](models/model.py#L415) |
| Balance weight | Coercion rule (fixed_uniform / base_only → 0.0) → CLI/API explicit value → layer default | [train.py](scripts/train.py#L74-L75), [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L324-L325), [model.py](models/model.py#L365-L366) |
| Test batch size | `--test-batch-size` → `--batch-size` | [train.py](scripts/train.py#L101) |
| Embedding file | `--embedding-file` → `EMBEDDING_FILES[data_name]` | [train.py](scripts/train.py#L102) |
| Checkpoint device placement | `--device`/`--device-ids` at load time → whatever was serialized in `config.pkl` is *ignored* | [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L370-L396) |
| Model hyperparameters at inference | All restored from `config.pkl`; CLI offers no overrides | [infer.py](scripts/infer.py#L61-L69) |

> [!TIP]
> The triple-layered coercion of `moe_balance_weight` is deliberate redundancy: even if a caller bypasses `scripts/train.py` and invokes `model_initialize` directly with a nonzero balance weight plus a control mode, `scPert_Model.__init__` (model.py#L365-L366) zeroes it again before the loss is ever computed in `_moe_balance_loss`.

Sources: [train.py](scripts/train.py#L71-L76), [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L320-L325), [model.py](models/model.py#L357-L368), [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L64-L77)

## Model Configuration Dictionary (`model_initialize`)

`scPert.model_initialize()` is the authoritative model configuration interface. Every key listed here enters the `self.config` dictionary, which is passed verbatim to `scPert_Model` and pickled to disk at save time. The first eight keys form the GEARS-inherited backbone configuration; the remaining MoE keys are the DyMoE-Pert additions. For a conceptual treatment of the fusion design itself, see [Residual Fusion Design](6-residual-fusion-design).

| Config key | API default | Serialized | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hidden_size` | 64 | Yes | Backbone width, MoE `output_dim`, embeddings, decoder |
| `embedding_size` | 512 (fixed) | Yes | scGPT embedding projection input |
| `num_go_gnn_layers` | 1 | Yes | GO graph GNN depth |
| `num_gene_gnn_layers` | 1 | Yes | Co-expression graph GNN depth |
| `decoder_hidden_size` | 16 | Yes | Gene-specific decoder width |
| `num_similar_genes_go_graph` | 20 | Yes | K in GO similarity graph |
| `num_similar_genes_co_express_graph` | 20 | Yes | K in co-expression similarity graph |
| `coexpress_threshold` | 0.4 | Yes | Pearson threshold for co-expression graph |
| `direction_lambda` | `1e-1` | Yes | Direction-loss regularization weight |
| `no_perturb` | `False` | Yes | Baseline no-perturbation mode |
| `use_moe_fusion` | `False` (CLI: `True`) | Yes | Builds `ResidualMoEFusion` when true |
| `moe_hidden_dim` | `None` → `hidden_size` | Yes | MoE hidden width |
| `moe_dropout` | 0.1 | Yes | Dropout in MoE submodules |
| `moe_balance_weight` | 0.01 (CLI: 0.0) | Yes | Balance-loss coefficient |
| `moe_router_mode` | `dynamic` | Yes | `dynamic` or `fixed_uniform` |
| `moe_ablation_mode` | `full` | Yes | Structural ablation selection |
| `moe_return_router_stats` | `True` | Yes | Emits `aux` router statistics dict |

Beyond these keys, the config dict also embeds runtime-derived values at initialization: `num_genes`, `num_perts`, the perturbation vocabulary (`pert_names`, `pert_node_map`), and `device`. These are derived from the loaded `PertData` and are therefore a function of your dataset, not free parameters. The class also exposes `tunable_parameters()`, a documentation method returning a dictionary describing the tunable backbone keys.

Sources: [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L250-L269), [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L271-L354), [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L327-L349)

## Checkpoint Configuration: `config.pkl` Round-Trip

The save/load pair is the reason inference is so spartan. `save_model` writes the *entire* config dictionary (including runtime-derived fields) to `config.pkl` alongside the state dict `model.pt`. On load, `load_pretrained` pops six keys that must be re-derived from the *current* data context rather than trusted from disk: `device`, `num_genes`, `num_perts`, `embedding_size`, `pert_names`, `pert_node_map`. It also defensively deletes legacy `uncertainty`/`uncertainty_reg` keys inherited from earlier scPert variants. Data-parallel state dicts are normalized by stripping the `module.` prefix, so checkpoints saved under `--multi-gpu` load identically on single GPU.

| Round-trip behavior | Detail |
|---|---|
| Saved artifact | `config.pkl` (full dict) + `model.pt` (unwrapped `best_model` state) |
| Restored keys | All `model_initialize` parameters (backbone + MoE) |
| Excluded on load | `device`, `num_genes`, `num_perts`, `embedding_size`, `pert_names`, `pert_node_map` |
| Legacy cleanup | `uncertainty`, `uncertainty_reg` deleted if present |
| Parallel prefix | `module.` stripped from state-dict keys |
| Device handling | Model moved to current `self.device`, not the saved one |

Sources: [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L357-L397), [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L399-L422)

> [!TIP]
> Because `load_pretrained` calls `model_initialize(**config)` internally, the checkpoint's `config.pkl` — not your CLI at inference time — is the single source of truth for architecture. Editing a checkpoint's `config.pkl` is the only way to alter a loaded model's structure; there are no inference-time CLI overrides.

## Data Pipeline Configuration

The `PertData` class carries its own small configuration surface, set at construction and at three method calls from `train.py` / `infer.py`.

**Constructor** — `PertData(data_path, gene_set_path=None, default_pert_graph=True)`: `data_path` is created if missing; `gene_set_path` overrides the default perturbation gene set (and implicitly disables the default graph); `default_pert_graph=True` triggers download of the full essential-gene list from Harvard Dataverse on first use.

Sources: [ProcePertdata.py](models/ProcePertdata.py#L60-L96), [ProcePertdata.py](models/ProcePertdata.py#L107-L126)

**Split configuration** — `prepare_split` accepts nine split strategies; `train.py` exposes only `--split` and `--seed` (77), leaving the remaining fraction parameters at their API defaults:

| Parameter | Default | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| `split` | `'simulation'` | Any of: `simulation`, `simulation_single`, `combo_seen0/1/2`, `single`, `no_test`, `no_split`, `custom` |
| `seed` | API 1 / CLI 77 | Deterministic split file naming and shuffling |
| `train_gene_set_size` | 0.75 | Fraction of gene set used for training (simulation splits) |
| `combo_seen2_train_frac` | 0.75 | Seen2 combo fraction for training |
| `combo_single_split_test_set_fraction` | 0.1 | Test fraction in combo/single splits |
| `test_perts` / `test_pert_genes` | `None` | Explicit test perturbation/gene lists |
| `only_test_set_perts` | `False` | Restrict testing to the given perts |
| `split_dict_path` | `None` | Required pickled dict for `split='custom'` |

Splits are cached as `{dataset}_{split}_{seed}_{train_gene_set_size}.pkl` under `<dataset_path>/splits/` — re-running with identical parameters reloads the cache instead of regenerating. The strategy semantics are covered in depth in [Perturbation Splits and Simulation Split](14-perturbation-splits-and-simulation-split).

Sources: [ProcePertdata.py](models/ProcePertdata.py#L268-L334), [ProcePertdata.py](models/ProcePertdata.py#L310-L314)

**Loader configuration** — `get_dataloader(batch_size, test_batch_size=None, use_data_list_loader=False)` selects `DataListLoader` when `use_data_list_loader` is true, which `train.py` ties to the `--multi-gpu` flag. Train loaders shuffle with `drop_last=True`; validation loaders shuffle without dropping; test loaders preserve order.

Sources: [ProcePertdata.py](models/ProcePertdata.py#L419-L491), [train.py](scripts/train.py#L119-L126)

## Inference Script CLI Reference

`scripts/infer.py` deliberately exposes only seven arguments. Model hyperparameters come exclusively from the checkpoint's `config.pkl`; the script always calls `prepare_split(split="no_test", seed=77)` because prediction needs only the control-cell pool, not the evaluation split.

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--checkpoint` | Yes | — | Directory containing `config.pkl` and `model.pt` |
| `--perturbation` | Yes | — | Format `GENE+ctrl` or `GENEA+GENEB` (e.g. `CEBPA+JUN`) |
| `--data-name` | No | `norman` | Selects dataset and embedding file via `EMBEDDING_FILES` |
| `--data-path` | No | `./data` | Dataset root |
| `--embedding-dir` | No | `./embeddings` | scGPT embedding directory |
| `--device` | No | `auto` | `auto` resolves to `cuda:0` if available, else `cpu` |
| `--num-cells` | No | 32 | Control cells sampled per prediction |
| `--batch-size` | No | 8 | Cells per inference forward pass |

Pre-flight validation checks positivity of `--num-cells`/`--batch-size`, CUDA availability when requested, and existence of all three required files (embedding, `config.pkl`, `model.pt`) — failing with a parser error rather than a mid-run traceback. Predictions are written as `pred_dymoe_{pert}.npz` in the working directory.

Sources: [infer.py](scripts/infer.py#L25-L54), [infer.py](scripts/infer.py#L56-L76), [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L424-L491)

## Hardcoded Architecture Constants

Not everything is configurable, and the fixed values are as important to reproducibility as the tunable ones. These constants are baked into `model.py` and cannot be changed via any documented argument:

| Constant | Value | Location / Role |
|---|---|---|
| `embedding_size` | 512 | scGPT embedding dimension; fixed in config dict |
| `kg_input_dim` | 128 | KG expert input width (from ComGCN KGE file) |
| `scgpt_input_dim` | 512 | scGPT expert input width |
| `num_experts` | 3 | Enforced; any other value raises in `ResidualMoEFusion` |
| Transformer depth / heads | 8 layers, `nhead=8` | Perturbation token transformer stack |
| Backbone dropout | 0.1 | Gene/pert dense blocks, transformer, final MLP |
| KG embedding file | `./embeddings/gene_2_kge_comgcn_final_common.npz` | Loaded by relative path in `scPert_Model` |
| Perturbation KGE file | `./embeddings/gene_embeddingss_full_common.npz` | Loaded by relative path in `scPert_Model` |
| Pert input concat dim | 640 (128 KG + 512 scGPT) | Width of `pert_dense` in non-MoE fallback path |

The relative-path loading of the two `.npz` files means the working directory must be the repository root when constructing `scPert_Model` — a hard constraint inherited from the embedding layout described in [Knowledge-Graph and scGPT Embeddings](13-knowledge-graph-and-scgpt-embeddings).

Sources: [model.py](models/model.py#L96-L110), [model.py](models/model.py#L371-L390), [model.py](models/model.py#L400-L445), [model.py](models/model.py#L467-L475)

## Training-Loop Configuration

The `train()` API signature sits between the CLI and the optimizer. Its defaults (`epochs=20`, `lr=0.002`, `weight_decay=1e-5`) differ from the CLI defaults (`25`, `0.001`) — when you run `scripts/train.py`, the CLI values always win because they are passed explicitly. Direct API users get the API defaults. The remaining two parameters, `use_parallel` and `device_ids`, are fully controlled by the `--multi-gpu`/`--device-ids` flags; the validation rules (minimum two GPUs, ids within range, first id must match `--device`) are enforced before training starts. GPU orchestration mechanics belong to [Multi-GPU Parallel Training](16-multi-gpu-parallel-training).

| `train()` parameter | API default | CLI-driven value |
|---|---|---|
| `epochs` | 20 | `--epochs` (25) |
| `lr` | 0.002 | `--lr` (0.001) |
| `weight_decay` | `1e-5` | Not exposed via CLI |
| `use_parallel` | `True` | `--multi-gpu` |
| `device_ids` | `None` | `--device-ids` |
| `key_genes` | `None` | Not exposed via CLI |

Sources: [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L533-L559), [train.py](scripts/train.py#L147)

## Quick-Start Configuration Recipes

The following canonical invocations illustrate how the precedence rules compose in practice. The default recipe trains on Norman with everything at defaults; the ablation recipes activate the control modes whose balance-weight coercion was described above; the multi-GPU recipe shows device-id pinning.

```bash
# Default: full MoE, dynamic router, simulation split, seed 77
python scripts/train.py

# Router ablation (fixed_uniform E3 control):
#   --moe-balance-weight is coerced to 0.0 regardless of what you pass
python scripts/train.py --moe-router-mode fixed_uniform --moe-balance-weight 0.05

# Structural ablation: experts without the residual base path
python scripts/train.py --moe-ablation-mode experts_only

# Custom embedding experiment (overrides dataset-aligned file)
python scripts/train.py --data-name adamson \
    --embedding-file gene_embeddings_norman_512.npy

# Multi-GPU on devices 0 and 1 (device must match first id)
python scripts/train.py --multi-gpu --device-ids 0,1 --device cuda:0

# Single-perturbation prediction from a trained checkpoint
python scripts/infer.py --checkpoint norman_model_FINAL \
    --perturbation CEBPA+JUN --num-cells 32
```

Sources: [train.py](scripts/train.py#L71-L93), [infer.py](scripts/infer.py#L61-L76)

## Configuration Decision Map

For quick diagnosis during experimentation, this map links each tuning goal to the authoritative parameter and its constraint:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Q{"What are you configuring?"}
    Q -->|Model width| H1["hidden_size<br/>(CLI + config.pkl)"]
    Q -->|MoE capacity| H2["moe_hidden_dim<br/>None → hidden_size"]
    Q -->|Router behavior| H3["moe_router_mode<br/>dynamic | fixed_uniform"]
    Q -->|Structure removal| H4["moe_ablation_mode<br/>full | base_only |<br/>no_interaction | experts_only"]
    Q -->|Balance regularization| H5["moe_balance_weight<br/>forced 0.0 in control modes"]
    Q -->|Evaluation protocol| H6["split + seed<br/>prepare_split cache key"]
    Q -->|Throughput| H7["batch-size / test-batch-size<br/>multi-gpu + device-ids"]
    Q -->|Restoring runs| H8["config.pkl<br/>no CLI overrides"]
```

Sources: [train.py](scripts/train.py#L21-L54), [scpert.py](models/scpert.py#L271-L354), [model.py](models/model.py#L415-L427)

## Summary and Next Steps

The configuration system of DyMoE-Pert follows a deliberate philosophy: a single serialized source of truth (`config.pkl`) for architecture, explicit CLI surface for training-time control, and triple-enforced invariants for the scientifically sensitive MoE control modes. The parameters you will touch most often — `hidden_size`, the four MoE switches, split/seed — flow through the chain unchanged; the ones you cannot touch (expert count, embedding dimensions, transformer depth) are fixed to keep checkpoints compatible and ablations comparable.

To go deeper from here:

- Understand what the MoE switches structurally change: [Ablation Modes Framework](9-ablation-modes-framework) and [Soft Router and Balance Loss](8-soft-router-and-balance-loss)
- Trace how `hidden_size` and `moe_hidden_dim` manifest in the fusion module: [Residual Fusion Design](6-residual-fusion-design)
- See how `--split` choices map to evaluation scenarios: [Perturbation Splits and Simulation Split](14-perturbation-splits-and-simulation-split)
- Follow a full command end-to-end: [Training and Prediction Commands](4-training-and-prediction-commands)

# Positioning vs GEARS and scPert



This page establishes where **DyMoE-Pert** sits relative to the two methodological ancestors it is measured against: **GEARS** (the graph-based perturbation modeling framework whose data ecosystem this repo adopts) and **scPert** (the knowledge-graph-embedding predecessor whose codebase this repository directly descends from). The positioning is built on three verifiable claims: the *data-and-metrics skeleton is inherited*, the *fusion layer is replaced with a dynamic residual MoE*, and *comparability with both baselines is preserved by construction* — same data files, same splits, same metric code. Throughout, we distinguish what the code proves from what the manuscript claims.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L5-L15), [scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L172-L175)

## A Three-Stage Methodological Lineage

The lineage is visible directly in the code, not inferred from papers. The training orchestration class is literally named `scPert` and self-describes as the "scPert base model class" ([scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L172-L175)); the neural network it drives is `scPert_Model` ([model.py](/models/model.py#L348-L350)). Meanwhile, the data layer speaks GEARS: `PertData` loads the GEARS-format `perturb_processed.h5ad` archives from Dataverse ([ProcePertdata.py](/models/ProcePertdata.py#L23-L58), [README.md](/README.md#L38-L46)), and `models/utils.py` carries the GEARS gene-graph machinery — `GeneSimNetwork`, GO-similarity edge construction via Jaccard overlap, and GO/co-expression network selection ([utils.py](/models/utils.py#L180-L208), [utils.py](/models/utils.py#L241-L265)). DyMoE-Pert is therefore not a from-scratch system: it is a fusion-layer intervention on top of an inherited scPert/GEARS skeleton.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    GEARS["GEARS conventions<br/>GEARS-format h5ad data, GO + co-expression<br/>graph utilities, DE-gene metric pipeline"]
    SCPERT["scPert (upstream release)<br/>class skeleton, training loop,<br/>predict / GI_predict API,<br/>ComGCN KGE + common 512-d embeddings"]
    SCGPT["scGPT checkpoint<br/>512-d embeddings generated<br/>per dataset by this project"]
    DYMOE["DyMoE-Pert (this repo)<br/>ResidualMoEFusion: KG expert,<br/>scGPT-slot expert, interaction expert,<br/>soft router + residual base branch"]

    GEARS -->|"data format, graph utilities,<br/>metric pipeline"| SCPERT
    SCPERT -->|"orchestration class scPert,<br/>PertData wiring"| DYMOE
    GEARS -->|"inherited evaluation<br/>conventions"| DYMOE
    SCPERT -->|"two common embedding files<br/>in ./embeddings/"| DYMOE
    SCGPT -->|"dataset-aligned gene_emb<br/>for the backbone"| DYMOE
```

The embedding provenance in the README makes the lineage explicit: `./embeddings/` contains "two common gene representations from the **upstream scPert repository**" (`gene_2_kge_comgcn_final_common.npz` and `gene_embeddingss_full_common.npz`) alongside "five dataset-aligned 512-dimensional arrays generated **for this project** from an scGPT checkpoint" ([README.md](/README.md#L50)). Inside `scPert_Model`, the ComGCN knowledge-graph file feeds the 128-dimensional KG slot and the common npz file feeds the 512-dimensional perturbation slot, while the project-generated scGPT arrays are loaded via `embedding_path` into `gene_emb`, the gene-token matrix consumed by the backbone ([model.py](/models/model.py#L370-L390), [model.py](/models/model.py#L651-L671)). Modality sourcing is covered in depth in [Knowledge-Graph and scGPT Embeddings](13-knowledge-graph-and-scgpt-embeddings).

Sources: [scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L172-L175), [model.py](/models/model.py#L348-L390), [ProcePertdata.py](/models/ProcePertdata.py#L23-L58), [utils.py](/models/utils.py#L180-L265), [README.md](/README.md#L38-L50)

## What Is Inherited: Data, Splits, and Metrics Infrastructure

Comparability with GEARS and scPert is not an aspiration — it is enforced by shared infrastructure. Every component needed to claim "we evaluated under identical conditions" already exists in the repo and is reused unchanged:

| Infrastructure component | In-repo location | Lineage role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GEARS-format `perturb_processed.h5ad` loader | `PertData` in [ProcePertdata.py](/models/ProcePertdata.py#L23-L58) | Identical processed archives as GEARS benchmarks (Norman, Adamson, Dixit, Replogle) |
| Simulation split machinery | `DataSplitter` via [data_utils.py](/models/data_utils.py#L1-L19), default seed 77 ([README.md](/README.md#L52-L54)) | Same unseen-perturbation protocol |
| DE-gene identification | `rank_genes_groups_by_cov`, `get_DE_genes` ([data_utils.py](/models/data_utils.py#L15-L70)) | GEARS differential-expression pipeline, unchanged |
| Evaluation metrics | `evaluate` / `compute_metrics` (MSE, Pearson on all genes and DE genes) in [inference.py](/models/inference.py#L42-L120) | GEARS-style metric definitions |
| Prediction API | `predict` / `GI_predict` on the `scPert` class ([scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L424-L530)) | Same programmatic surface an scPert user already knows |

This shared skeleton means the only experimental variable between an scPert-style run and a DyMoE-Pert run is the model configuration — principally the `use_moe_fusion` switch and its router/ablation parameters ([model.py](/models/model.py#L357-L368), [scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L271-L349)). Determinism is also anchored identically: `torch.manual_seed(0)` is set at module import in `scpert.py` ([scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L26-L26)), matching the fixed-seed convention documented for benchmark runs ([README.md](/README.md#L52-L54)). Split semantics themselves are detailed in [Perturbation Splits and Simulation Split](14-perturbation-splits-and-simulation-split), and the metrics in [Metrics and DE Gene Analysis](18-metrics-and-de-gene-analysis).

Sources: [ProcePertdata.py](/models/ProcePertdata.py#L23-L58), [data_utils.py](/models/data_utils.py#L15-L70), [inference.py](/models/inference.py#L42-L120), [scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L26-L26), [scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L271-L349), [README.md](/README.md#L52-L54)

## What Is Replaced: From Fixed Fusion to Dynamic Residual MoE

The decisive architectural break with both ancestors is *how modalities are combined*. The lineage offers three fusion patterns, and all three are inspectable in this repository:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph FIXED["Pattern A - fixed fusion (scPert-style, retained in repo)"]
        A1["128-d ComGCN KGE"] --> A2["concat + pert_dense MLP"]
        A3["512-d pert embedding"] --> A2
    end
    subgraph DYN["Pattern B - dynamic fusion (DyMoE-Pert)"]
        B1["128-d KGE<br/>kg_projector"] --> B4{"soft router"}
        B2["512-d embedding<br/>scgpt_projector"] --> B4
        B3["interaction features<br/>z_kg, z_sc, z_kg*z_sc, abs diff"] --> B4
        B5["residual base branch<br/>base_mlp"] --> B6["weighted expert sum<br/>+ LayerNorm"]
        B4 --> B6
    end
```

Pattern A is not hypothetical: it is the live code path taken when `use_moe_fusion=False`, where `_fuse_pert_embedding` simply concatenates the two embeddings and passes them through the static `pert_dense` MLP ([model.py](/models/model.py#L478-L481)). Pattern B instantiates `ResidualMoEFusion` with exactly three experts — KG, scGPT-slot, and cross-modal interaction — a learned soft router over the projected base input, and a residual base branch carrying shared multimodal information ([model.py](/models/model.py#L96-L167), [model.py](/models/model.py#L418-L429)). This is precisely the README's positioning statement made concrete: "Rather than applying one fixed fusion rule to every perturbation, DyMoE-Pert learns how much to use each" source per input ([README.md](/README.md#L9-L11)).

> [!TIP]
> The fixed-fusion baseline used to justify the MoE does not require an external scPert implementation — flipping `use_moe_fusion` to `False` runs the scPert-style concatenation path inside the *same* model, data loader, and metric harness, eliminating harness-induced confounds from the comparison.

| Dimension | GEARS conventions (inherited data layer) | scPert-style path (`use_moe_fusion=False`) | DyMoE-Pert (`use_moe_fusion=True`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Perturbation identity | Effect propagated over GO/co-expression gene graphs | Fixed embedding per perturbed gene | Fixed embedding per perturbed gene |
| External knowledge | GO + co-expression network construction ([utils.py](/models/utils.py#L241-L265)) | ComGCN KGE (128-d) as a static feature | ComGCN KGE (128-d) — but routed, not concatenated |
| Second modality | None | 512-d common perturbation embedding, concat-fused | 512-d embedding + learned cross-modal interaction expert |
| Fusion rule | Graph message passing | Static concat + MLP | Input-dependent soft-router weights + residual base branch |
| Prediction target | Delta over control expression | Delta over control expression ([model.py](/models/model.py#L754-L755)) | Delta over control expression ([model.py](/models/model.py#L754-L755)) |

The GEARS-heritage claim for the first column rests on what the code retains: GEARS pert-string parsing (`GENE1+GENE2`, `ctrl` handling), GO-graph edge lists with Jaccard scores above 0.1, and K-nearest-neighbor pruning of similarity networks are all live utilities ([utils.py](/models/utils.py#L16-L39), [utils.py](/models/utils.py#L197-L208)). Fusion internals are the territory of [Residual Fusion Design](6-residual-fusion-design) and [Expert Specialization: KG, scGPT, Interaction](7-expert-specialization-kg-scgpt-interaction); router mechanics belong to [Soft Router and Balance Loss](8-soft-router-and-balance-loss).

Sources: [model.py](/models/model.py#L96-L167), [model.py](/models/model.py#L418-L429), [model.py](/models/model.py#L478-L481), [model.py](/models/model.py#L651-L671), [utils.py](/models/utils.py#L16-L39), [utils.py](/models/utils.py#L197-L265), [README.md](/README.md#L9-L11)

## What the Backbone Does Instead of GEARS-Style GNN Propagation

GEARS-derived configuration knobs survive in the API surface — `tunable_parameters` still advertises `num_go_gnn_layers`, `num_gene_gnn_layers`, `decoder_hidden_size`, `num_similar_genes_go_graph`, `coexpress_threshold`, and `direction_lambda` ([scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L250-L269)), and `model_initialize` accepts them into the config dict ([scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L271-L349)). However, the module that actually consumes `config` — `scPert_Model.__init__` — builds none of them. No GO-GNN, no co-expression-GNN, and no gene-specific decoder are constructed; instead the forward path builds a shared transformer stack of eight `ImprovedTransformerLayer` blocks ([model.py](/models/model.py#L442-L445)), computes gene-gene interaction as scaled-dot-product attention over projected gene tokens with a softmax-weighted context aggregation ([model.py](/models/model.py#L684-L693)), and predicts through a global `final_mlp` + `output_layer` head with a half-scaled residual per transformer block ([model.py](/models/model.py#L743-L754)).

> [!TIP]
> The legacy GEARS hyperparameters (`num_go_gnn_layers`, `decoder_hidden_size`, `direction_lambda`, …) are stored in `config.pkl` but are dead settings in this codebase — `scPert_Model.__init__` never reads them. Tuning them will change nothing; the effective control surface is the `moe_*` parameters and `hidden_size`.

The class-level interaction below shows the full inheritance-and-extension wiring at runtime — useful when tracing where a comparison run diverges from its scPert equivalent:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PD["PertData<br/>GEARS-format loading, splits,<br/>node maps"] -->|"dataloader, adata,<br/>pert_list"| SP["scPert<br/>orchestration: train, predict,<br/>GI_predict, MoE balance loss"]
    SP -->|"model_initialize config<br/>incl. moe_* switches"| SM["scPert_Model<br/>gene tokens, transformer backbone,<br/>control-residual head"]
    SM -->|"kg_embedding + 512-d pert embedding<br/>only if use_moe_fusion"| MOE["ResidualMoEFusion<br/>3 experts, soft router,<br/>ablation modes"]
    MOE -->|"fused embedding +<br/>router aux dict"| SM
    SM -->|"pred, moe_aux"| SP
    SP -->|"results"| INF["inference.py<br/>evaluate, compute_metrics,<br/>GEARS-style DE analysis"]
    SP -->|"base_loss + balance_weight *<br/>balance_loss"| OPT["AdamW + OneCycleLR"]
```

One GEARS convention survives in the *output contract* rather than the architecture: like GEARS, the model predicts a correction on top of measured control expression rather than absolute expression — the final reshape adds the input control vector `x` to the network output ([model.py](/models/model.py#L754-L757)). This keeps the semantic of "perturbation effect" consistent across all three methods and is what makes the downstream DE-gene comparisons directly interpretable.

Sources: [scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L250-L269), [scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L271-L349), [model.py](/models/model.py#L442-L445), [model.py](/models/model.py#L684-L693), [model.py](/models/model.py#L743-L757), [scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L64-L77)

## Claim Boundaries: What This Repository Does and Does Not Establish

An honest positioning statement requires boundaries, and the README supplies them explicitly. This repository provides "the **core runnable implementation**" — model, loader, train/predict commands, and runtime embedding files — but "does not include expression datasets, trained checkpoints, experiment logs, or scripts for reproducing every manuscript table" ([README.md](/README.md#L13-L15)). Consequently, this codebase lets you *replicate the comparison protocol* (shared data, splits, metrics), but the published GEARS/scPert baseline numbers come from the accompanying manuscript, not from runnable baseline scripts shipped here.

The manuscript's own positioning is deliberately conservative: performance "varies by dataset and metric," with "the clearest reported advantage ... for the challenging combinations in which neither constituent gene was" seen during training ([README.md](/README.md#L13-L13)). For intermediate developers, the practical reading is: DyMoE-Pert is positioned as a *fusion-strategy upgrade with the strongest expected gain in the unseen-combination regime*, not as a universal winner across every dataset–metric cell. The ablation framework (`full`, `base_only`, `no_interaction`, `experts_only`) exists precisely to attribute gains to specific experts rather than to the MoE wrapper generically ([model.py](/models/model.py#L109-L117), [scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L86-L99)) — see [Ablation Modes Framework](9-ablation-modes-framework). To run predictions yourself, start from [Quick Start](2-quick-start) and [Training and Prediction Commands](4-training-and-prediction-commands), and consult [Configuration Reference](19-configuration-reference) for the `moe_*` switches.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L13-L15), [model.py](/models/model.py#L109-L117), [scpert.py](/models/scpert.py#L86-L99)
